title: Strange Gazes
subtitle: Soldiers. Heads lowered. Lips sealed with orders.

trails.title: Fool or Genius?
trails.description: I sincerely hope returning time doesn't become some new form of competition.

content.text:
Fiddler Crab Shapeshifting for Dummies
—Call Number: F-4312-A
—Category: Shapeshifting - Marine Critter Biology Branch

Borrowing Record
Sonetto: Returned after 2 hours and 36 minutes.
Hans Levis: Returned after one week.
...
Cyril Aman: Returned the following day at the same time (abandoned practice, claiming to hear the sound of tsunamis in their nightmares).
Lark von Stuhr: Returned after 5 days and 6 hours.
Merel: Returned after 2 days and 3 hours.

*Librarian's Note:
Aside from Sonetto and Merel, all returns showed claw marks along the spine and traces of salt residue.
Going forward, this book may only be borrowed under teacher supervision.

items.text: Strange Gazes
Thousands of warhorses carrying fully armed cavalrymen travel to Tamarovka, their heavy hooves pounding the dirt road into hard-packed earth.
The Cavalry Corps's reconnaissance team reaches the village first. The villagers are on alert, eyeing the soldiers from their doorways.
Tamarovka

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: You heard, Merel? A Foundation big shot's coming to the village. That's a first!

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Big shot? Who?
Merel unconsciously reaches for her mask, suddenly realizing that she lost it during her escape.

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: Not sure, but the commander needs to welcome them personally. *sigh* Forget it. None of our business.

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: Natash—huh?
As they pass a nearby house, Sergey seems to spot an old acquaintance in a doorway. He leans forward to greet her, but she shuts the door in his face.
The hostility radiating from the onlookers in every direction makes Merel want to curl into a ball.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Um, Sergey, isn't this your hometown? Why are they staring at you like that?

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: I don't know. It's not like I've made that many enemies. Just one or two at most.

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: Anyway, let's go meet my uncle. See that house with the iron sheeting? That's our home.
Merel follows his finger to a house with a blue iron-sheet roof. A man holding a cane stands in the yard.
Sergey takes off his hat and excitedly waves it in the air.

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: Uncle Petro!
The old man only strikes the ground with his cane. His heavy blink seems to say, "Don't start, boy."

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: What's going on?

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Maybe something happened? Should we go ask him?
Sergey never expected his return home to be so dispirited. His uncle pulls him aside. Merel follows behind.

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: What's wrong, Uncle Petro?

items.speaker: Sergey's Uncle
items.text: You tell me! Did your commander say you'd fight those bandits or not?

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: Of course!

items.speaker: Sergey's Uncle
items.text: When?

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: That-That I don't know. It's a military secret!

items.speaker: Sergey's Uncle
items.text: Word is you're going to the city—the lot of you! So where does that leave the rest of us, hm? The villagers need protecting too!
The young man can't think of an answer. He can only stand in awkward silence. The uncle sighs and grips his nephew's shoulder hard with a slim yet powerful hand.

items.speaker: Sergey's Uncle
items.text: Alright, Seryozha, I understand. Everything's packed and ready to go. Come, we're leaving to your cousin's in Petrovka.

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: Uncle Petro! Could you just tell me what's going on? I'm not deserting Zeno!
Sergey shakes off his uncle's hand. The old man's neck flushes red with embarrassment and anger. He turns and glances at Merel.

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: It's fine. She's a friend.

items.speaker: Sergey's Uncle
items.text: The cavalry is leaving us here to die. And the refugees from upstream—they said there are tens of thousands of bandits up there.

items.speaker: Sergey's Uncle
items.text: I don't know where they all came from, but your cavalry's nothing compared to that, right? You'll never fight them all off.

items.speaker: Sergey's Uncle
items.text: And keep this quiet, but the kolduny left and joined the bandits!

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: What?

items.speaker: Sergey's Uncle
items.text: Tch-tch-tch! They said they'd punish anyone who stands with the cavalry when they return.
He watches the Cavalry Corps soldiers passing by the village entrance.

items.speaker: Sergey's Uncle
items.text: If you can't fight them off, they'll burn the village to ashes. So, are you coming with us? Yes or no?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I see Lilya.
A small group of reinforcements makes its slow advance across the grassland. A transport team carrying guns and artillery rumbles close behind.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Hmm. That must be the commander of the Zeno cavalry beside her.
The Cavalry Corps officers awaiting them ride out to the head of the team to guide them to their destination.
Before the commander can reach them, an old friend steps forward to greet the Timekeeper.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Captain! Why did the Foundation send you here? Isn't exactly the safest place in the world right now.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I applied for it. There's something I need to find in Bereggrad.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Don't give me that look, Lilya. Madam Z approved it.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Alright, what Z says goes.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: I'm glad to see you safe and sound, Ms. Lilya. Your message had us worried.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Hah. The Foundation seriously needs to update their communication devices. At least, make them bulletproof.
The commander approaches as they chat.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Timekeeper.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Commander Ivan, it's a pleasure to meet you. If you could, a brief walk-through of the situation in Bereggrad and the surrounding areas would be most helpful.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Of course. But tell me, where did that company behind you spring from? I received no word in our communications.
The commander's eyes settle on a small detachment within the reinforcements, about a hundred soldiers strong, led by a red-haired knight.
The knight notices him, too. She dismounts and steps forward.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: Vice Admiral Burakov, I am the medic of the Foundation's special unit "XII." Behind me are the soldiers returning from the front lines and our field medical team.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: Every one of them is willing to enlist in the cavalry and join the fight against the bandits.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Good to know.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Go to Colonel Sabina Sternova. She will see your men settled.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: Yes, Commander.
The knight leads the special unit away.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Follow me, if you will, Timekeeper.
Indoors

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Intelligence has spoken: the scattered bandit forces are converging upstream of the Don. They carry Zeno weaponry, though their identity is yet unknown.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Most likely, this is Igor's doing, though we've kept clear of them thus far, as headquarters ordered.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Villages have been plundered. Many have fled downstream, yet most cling to their homes.
The commander lifts his eyes from the map, still deep in thought.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Zeno has ordered the cavalry station in Bereggrad until your mission is complete. We ride at dawn.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Many of your cavalrymen are locals from the era. What do they think of Igor?

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: What happened in São Paulo is classified. To them, he's a warlord like any other.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: We do have a controlled route to the city, but Timekeeper, are you certain you wish to enter? The rebels could strike at any moment.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Yes. I'll complete my mission quickly, hopefully before any conflict arises.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: I see. Then tell me the details of your mission so that I may lend my hand.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: There's a place in the city called the Amber Room. It's said to hold an important clue about the "Storm."

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Does it sound familiar at all, Commander?

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Not the Amber Room in St. Petersburg, I presume. We're a long way off from there.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Then no, can't say it does. It seems I cannot aid you much in this.
The commander pauses, then asks the question that's been gnawing at him since the Timekeeper's arrival.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Timekeeper, may I ask: besides your "Storm" investigation, are you also here to deal with the Golden Famine?

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: We tried ourselves, but Zeno soldiers have little experience in arcane matters. We couldn't unearth the root.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I'm sorry. I didn't receive any information on that matter. But I'll keep an eye out for you.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: I see.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: The cavalry will aid you in any way we can. But with our strength as it is, I cannot guarantee the safety of Bereggrad.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I'm not sure how much it will help, but I heard reinforcements are on the way.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: The newly formed Flying Witch Company will arrive soon, along with a new broomstick for Lilya.
Lilya suddenly perks up.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Zeno reformed the Flying Witches?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: No, this unit belongs to the Foundation.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Lilya, Committee member Irinei asks if you'll serve as its temporary captain. What do you say?
Sternova gestures to a lonely, empty house.

items.speaker: Sternova
items.text: We haven't seen the owner of this place for two years. The elder said you can stay here for a few days.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: This is spacious.
If you ignore its decrepit state, it is a fairly decent place for a short stay.

items.speaker: Sternova
items.text: Um, yeah. The stable in the yard still needs some fixing up, so the cavalry will have to take care of your horse, if you don't mind.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: That would be kind of you. Thank you very much.

items.speaker: Sternova
items.text: It's no big deal. What's one more horse to feed?
Sternova hands the key to Marsha and leads her horse away.
Just as Marsha is about to slip the key inside the lock, a rustling sound catches her attention.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: Is that a rat?
Not the sound a rat would make.
A small black shadow vanishes behind the once-leafy elm in the corner of the yard.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: Hm? Or a child from the village?

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: Never mind. I need to rest.
She hears it again. She looks over to the same spot.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: Who's there?
From behind the elm, a head peeks out, briefly meeting her eyes.
This time, the shadow doesn't hide itself behind the tree but disappears in the glow of an arcane skill.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: Vanished? Just like that?
This could be a threat. Marsha draws her weapon and moves toward the fading arcane light.
A shadow flashes past once more.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: What? That was definitely a person.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: A person sneaking in the shadows around the cavalry's station. Suspicious to be sure. A spy, perhaps?
*a strange sound*
Its direction is exposed again.
Turning, Marsha stares intently.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: Are my eyes playing tricks on me? Is that a fiddler crab? On the Don steppe?
The knight runs toward the dubious fiddler crab at astonishing speed. Her heavy armor doesn't seem to slow her down in the slightest.
In its desperation, her opponent flees sideways toward the outskirts of the village.
But there is no escape. The knight is closing in on the crab.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: Got you!
Forced into a corner, the fiddler crab snaps its oversized claws in the air.

items.speaker: Fiddler Crab?
items.text: Sssss, ssss!

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: Enough, shapeshifter! This is absurd! How would a fiddler crab make it out here to the plain?

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: And might I remind you that you're too big to be a crab?

items.speaker: Fiddler Crab?
items.text: Sss ...
The same glow returns, the light surrounding the fiddler crab bending and distorting.
It reveals the figure of a girl.
The newly appointed medic of the "XII" Squad locks eyes with her team's deserter.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: H-Hey, nice to see you again. Heh.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: Merel?

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: H-How did you ...
Marsha steps forward. Caught at last, Merel squats down, covering her head with both hands.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: D-Don't hurt me! I'll tell you everything.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: You mean to say you plan to stay here until the war's over?

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Well, I don't really have much choice. At least with the cavalry, I won't starve.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: And if the "Storm" comes? What then?

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: I'll be fine. I took an Equilibrium Umbrella with me. And maybe in the next era, I'll find a safer place to stay.
Her face sinks.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Oh. Oh no. I lost it when the bandits chased me.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Oourgh!
The knight grabs her face with both hands, pressing her cheeks tight together.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Let go.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: This is serious, Merel! Do you have any idea what they do to deserters? Do you think hiding with Zeno will prevent the Foundation from finding you?

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: I ... I don't know.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: You may survive one "Storm," but what about the next? And the others after that?

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Please ... Marsha ...

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: How will you know which era the "Storm" will take us to next?

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Marsha ... Can't ... breathe ...
She lets go.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: Honestly! What am I to do with you?
Merel hangs her head, rubbing her reddened cheeks.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: So, why are you here?

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: I was taking a group of Don Cossacks home and heard the Timekeeper was going the same direction, so we met on the road and traveled the rest of the way together.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: Now that I have arrived, Creius has requested I stay by the Timekeeper's side until she completes her mission. Then I'll return with her.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Y-You're not going to bring me back to Creius, are you?
Marsha leans against a worn pillar, looking deeply downcast.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: If only I could. But with Creius comes the Foundation. Either way, I'll be sure to bring you back. Running around alone out here is far more dangerous than anything the Foundation could do.
Merel knows there's nothing left she can do.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: Does anybody else here know you, aside from me?

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: No.
The image of the young Foundation "big shot" appears in Merel's mind. She shakes her head, trying to erase those gray eyes from her memory.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: I know the Timekeeper and Lieutenant Lilya, but I don't think they know me.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: But Sonetto, Vertin's assistant ... I'm not so sure. We were classmates for a few years, but we didn't talk much.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: I see. Stay close with me, then, and don't let Sonetto see you. It would be best if we solved this without any interference from a third party.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: Paravyan and I may be able to plead your case, but if we're to have any chance of being successful, you can't run away. Not again.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Urgh!
A sharp noise breaks the silence, startling the still-nervy Merel. She jerks her head up but sees only a few swirling trails of condensation lingering in the sky.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: What is that?
Marsha looks up too, but she shows no sign of alarm.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: It's the Foundation's flight unit. They're here.
